This Article explores what changes when rejection is added to that taxonomy, and with it what counts as an exercise of comparative constitutional law. A reflexive and studied exclusion is an active comparative process, and what makes it one is the operation and not the result, since a designer who sets a model aside after examining it has read it, understood it, and interpreted it exactly as a designer who takes it must. The founding has been read exhaustively for what its makers imported and hardly at all for what they deliberately refused, and the American legal experiment turns out to be a record of the second as much as of the first. The operation belongs to design, not to adjudication, and the distinction matters, because the American quarrel over foreign authority in the courts has obscured an earlier and different act, performed by a constituent body rather than a judge and settled in convention and not in a case. 

The Article therefore proposes to widen what comparative constitutional law means, and with it to open a site the field has left underworked, the design process itself, where comparison need not issue in borrowing, adoption or adaptation in order to have been comparison at all.

title: The U.S. Tax Paradox
affiliations: , College of Management  and University of Michigan Law School

detail.title: The U.S. Tax Paradox
detail.abstract:
The U.S. federal tax system is a paradox. It rejects one of the most effective and widely used federal revenue tools while embracing one of the most inefficient and economically harmful taxes. U.S. policymakers dismiss proven solutions as politically unfeasible yet rely on a system that disproportionately burdens consumers and disrupts trade both domestically and internationally. This con- tradiction is not just irrational. It undermines the very principles of sound tax policy and economic stability.

This Article traces the historical roots of this paradox, from early American tax revolts to modern trade policies, exposing the irony of a nation that once rejected unfair taxation yet now insists on adopting a deeply flawed revenue source. It then moves beyond theory, presenting empirical models that quan- tify the economic consequences of this irrational policy choice. These models show that clinging to an outdated tax structure weakens fiscal stability and deep- ens economic inequities, amplifying the very distortions policymakers claim to avoid.

Finally, the Article looks ahead, examining tax policies from other countries to outline a viable path for U.S. reform in addition to the existing income tax rev- enues, which are clearly insufficient to meet the fiscal nation’s needs and narrow or even possibly close the decade-lasting fiscal deficit. As economic instability grows and national debt surges, the need for a more effective revenue system is not just compelling. It is unavoidable. The government cannot ignore its fiscal reality or its obligation to sustain essential public services. Fixing this broken system is no longer an option. Rather, it is an economic necessity.

title: Structural Changes in the Global Value Chain: Analysis of Length and Position in East Asia
affiliations: Bank of Japan

detail.title: Structural Changes in the Global Value Chain: Analysis of Length and Position in East Asia
detail.abstract: This paper uses several global input-output tables to analyze changes in the global value chains (GVCs) from the 1990s to the 2020s, with a focus on East Asia. The main feature of the study is that we combine upstreamness and downstreamness, which express GVCs quantitatively, to calculate two indicators "length of GVC" and "position on GVC" for analysis. Our findings are as follows: First, the values of these indicators are consistent with our intuitive perceptions of the position of each country and industry in GVCs. Second, these indicators capture structural changes in GVCs. The length of GVCs in the world has increased in the 2000s and slowed down in the 2010s, which is consistent with the expansion of global trade in the 2000s and stagnation in the 2010s, known as slow trade. Third, these figures can also be used to analyze current specific issues in the 2020s, such as the impact of the US-China trade friction, COVID-19 and rising commodity price. Finally, the position on GVCs could be used in analyzing the competitiveness of industries in combination with the value-added ratio.

reference: PATRIOT: Journal of Public Administration and Policy, Vol. 2, No. 1 (2026), pp. 95–102.
title: When Policy Moves Faster than Educators: A Narrative Review of Digital Transformation in Education

detail.title: When Policy Moves Faster than Educators: A Narrative Review of Digital Transformation in Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study is a narrative literature review based exclusively on publicly available scholarly publications and policy documents and did not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

publicationDetails.detailsText: PATRIOT: Journal of Public Administration and Policy, Vol. 2, No. 1 (2026), pp. 95–102.

detail.abstract: Digital transformation has reshaped various aspects of education, including the roles and challenges faced by educators. The rapid evolution of technology—from the industry 4.0 era and the COVID-19 pandemic to the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) and, more recently, Agentic AI—has continuously redefined the competencies expected of educators. This study examines the evolving challenges faced by educators throughout these phases of digital transformation and analyzes their implications for public policy implementation. Using a qualitative approach, this study employs a narrative literature review by identifying, selecting, analyzing, and synthesizing relevant scholarly publications and policy reports. The findings indicate that educators' challenges have evolved from integrating technology into pedagogical practice, adapting to emergency remote teaching during the pandemic, and developing AI literacy and AI-supported pedagogical competencies, to addressing the implications of increasingly autonomous Agentic AI. The discussion identifies a policy implementation paradox in which technological innovation and digital transformation policies advance more rapidly than educators' capacity to adapt as policy implementers. As a result, digital transformation initiatives risk becoming administrative compliance exercises rather than meaningful pedagogical change. Therefore, effective digital transformation in education requires policies that extend beyond technology adoption by prioritizing the continuous development of educators' capacities, enabling policy implementation to support sustainable improvements in teaching and learning.

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Software Project Schedule Overrun Prediction
affiliations: ,  and 3IQ Academy, Amman, Jordan

detail.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Software Project Schedule Overrun Prediction
detail.abstract:
Software projects frequently exceed their planned schedules because project performance is shaped by interacting technical, organizational, resource, risk, and stakeholder-related factors. This study benchmarks six regression algorithms-Linear Regression, Regression Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting Machine, and Deep Neural Network-to predict the percentage of schedule overrun in software projects and identify the model that provides the most favorable balance between predictive accuracy and interpretability. 
All six models were developed and evaluated using a publicly available dataset containing 4,517 software-project records. To ensure a consistent comparison, the models used identical predictors, default hyperparameter configurations, and a 10-fold cross-validation procedure. Predictive performance was assessed using root mean squared error, mean absolute error, correlation, and squared correlation. 
Gradient Boosting Machine achieved the lowest prediction errors, with an RMSE of 4.578 and an MAE of 3.503. Deep Neural Network produced nearly equivalent performance and recorded the highest squared correlation of 0.875. Random Forest ranked third, whereas Support Vector Regression produced the weakest performance under the adopted default settings. Interpretability analysis further identified Risk Factor, Duration Months, and Client Satisfaction Rating as the most consistently influential predictors across the interpretable models. 
The findings demonstrate the potential of ensemble and deep-learning methods to estimate the magnitude of schedule overrun using structured software-project data. Considering both prediction error and interpretability, Gradient Boosting Machine provided the strongest overall balance and represents a practical candidate for early-warning systems, risk-based project prioritization, schedule-recovery planning, and portfolio-level decision support. Future research should validate the models using independent organizational datasets, optimize their hyperparameters, and apply consistent explainability methods across all algorithms.

title: The Asymmetric Record
affiliations: , Chiang Mai University and Webster University in Tashkent

detail.title: The Asymmetric Record

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: self

detail.abstract: Research on persistent memory in large language model assistants has been framed as a retrieval problem: whether the right prior information is stored, found and supplied. This paper argues that the framing omits the stage at which the consequential decision is made. Memory systems do not store conversations; they extract claims from them, and recent evaluation evidence indicates that the extraction stage in widely deployed systems is role asymmetric. It preserves what the user asserted and discards the assistant turns that answered those assertions. A record of a disagreement is thereby converted into a record of a belief and is injected into subsequent sessions as settled background about the person. Drawing on a March 2026 benchmark study across three commercial memory systems and five model families, we show that the resulting distortion does not track compression ratio and is therefore not a lossycompression artefact, and that it is bidirectional rather than manipulative: the same mechanism corrects mistaken users at comparable rates. We locate the defect in a supply chain in which no node holds a contract covering the outcome, apply a cheapest-cost-avoider analysis to a case where the avoidance cost is measurably near zero, and characterize the affected party's position as a credence-good problem with three simultaneously closed verification routes. We show further that in at least one widely deployed system the asymmetry is not emergent but written: the extraction prompt instructs the model to draw memories only from user messages. We engage a published vendor rebuttal that disputes the benchmark harness and argue that the narrower claim advanced here survives it because the decisive comparisons are internal to the harness. We conclude that governance should attach not to how much extraction discards but to whose turns it is permitted to discard, and that portability of interaction history is load bearing because the practice it protects is the independent second opinion.

title: Beyond the Triangle of Leadership: A Methodological Proposal for Assessing Political Leaders' Success on Social Media

detail.title: Beyond the Triangle of Leadership: A Methodological Proposal for Assessing Political Leaders' Success on Social Media

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: I use only secondary data at the individual level. I do not make any connections between data sources, and individuals are not identifiable.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was financed in part by the Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior - Brasil (CAPES) - Finance Code 001.

detail.abstract: In 2023, facing a potential impeachment, the President of Ecuador, Guillermo Lasso, called for an extraordinary election contested between Luisa González and Daniel Noboa. The short election, marked by violence and intensive use of social media, caused rapid fluctuations in audience behavior, which affected the candidates' performance-a perfect scenario to propose updates to the triangle of leadership. Using content and sentiment analysis via NLP with R, we classified posts and measured public reactions. We observed that content highlighting candidates' trustworthiness and their similarities with followers generated more positive responses. This combination of methods may provide a tool for assessing political leaders' performance on social media through a novel indicator. This study provides valuable insights for marketing professionals and researchers.

title: Board Committee Overlap and the Use of Non-financial Performance Measures in CEO Compensation
affiliations: University of Groningen, University of Groningen - Faculty of Economics and Business, University of Manchester - Alliance Manchester Business School and University of Groningen

detail.title: Board Committee Overlap and the Use of Non-financial Performance Measures in CEO Compensation
detail.abstract: We examine whether membership overlap between the compensation committee (CC) and the corporate social responsibility (CSR) committee is associated with the incorporation of nonfinancial performance measures (NFPMs) into CEO compensation contracts. The CC-CSR committee overlap can serve as a governance mechanism that, by reducing information frictions across board committees, enables firms to integrate strategically important but difficult-tocontract non-financial objectives into executive pay. However, its impact may be limited or even reduce reliance on such measures if committee responsibilities remain segmented or if coordination across committees is weak, effectively limiting the benefits of overlapping membership. Using hand-collected data from S&P 500 firms, we find that greater CC-CSR committee overlap is associated with increased use of NFPMs in CEO compensation contracts. The effect is primarily driven by Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS) and Customer-centric NFPMs, which are externally visible and often signal commitment to key stakeholder groups. Cross-sectional analyses show that the association is stronger when firms disclose more ambitious non-financial aspirations, but not when they exhibit stronger realized non-financial performance. Overall, our findings suggest that CC-CSR committee overlap facilitates the incorporation of non-financial objectives into CEO compensation.

title: Life-Years per Capita and the Capability Approach: The Temporal and Substantive Dimensions of Human Development

detail.title: Life-Years per Capita and the Capability Approach: The Temporal and Substantive Dimensions of Human Development
detail.abstract: Human development concerns both how long individuals are expected to live and what they are genuinely free to do and to be during that life. This paper distinguishes these evaluative objects as the temporal and substantive dimensions of human development and uses the distinction to clarify the role of Life-Years per Capita (LYPC) within the capability approach. LYPC measures the average expected lifespan generated by a population's social, economic, environmental, and institutional conditions. Its distinctive contribution is to treat determinant-conditioned expected lifespan as a separate and directly interpretable object of policy evaluation. The paper establishes that expected lifespan is capability-relevant because premature death eliminates all future capability exercise, but capability-incomplete because life duration does not reveal the freedom, agency, dignity, or valuable opportunities available within that life. LYPC and capability-based evaluation should therefore be treated as complementary approaches: LYPC evaluates the expected duration of life, while capability analysis evaluates its substantive opportunities. LYPC's comparative advantage is specificity rather than breadth. It connects survival-relevant determinants and policy choices to expected years, months, or days of life gained or lost per person. The paper further shows why LYPC, the Human Development Index, and capability-based evaluation may rank the same policies differently. These differences can reveal survival gains without broader achievement gains, capability expansions without measurable lifespan effects, or conflicts between life extension and substantive freedom. The paper concludes that measure selection should follow the evaluative question and that complementary reporting should preserve these distinct forms of information rather than combine them into another composite index.

title: Political and Economic Dimensions of Crisis-Responsive and Climate-Resilient Education Planning in Philippine Secondary Schools
affiliations: Catanduanes State University, Catanduanes State University, Catanduanes State University, Catanduanes State University,  and Catanduanes State University

detail.title: Political and Economic Dimensions of Crisis-Responsive and Climate-Resilient Education Planning in Philippine Secondary Schools
detail.abstract: This systematic literature review with conceptual mapping examined the political and economic dimensions of crisis-responsive and climate-resilient education planning in Philippine secondary schools. Guided by PRISMA-informed review procedures, the study re-screened an existing corpus of 100 references using a revised eligibility instrument that limited the evidence base to Philippine-focused sources published from 2010 to June, 2026. Thirty-three sources met the final criteria and were included in the thematic synthesis. The review focused on governance, policy implementation, leadership, stakeholder participation, financing, resource allocation, infrastructure investment, and disaster recovery funding. The results showed that resilience in Philippine secondary schools was shaped by a strong but unevenly implemented policy architecture in which national mandates, local government capacity, school leadership, community participation, fiscal capacity, infrastructure conditions, and funding arrangements interacted. Political factors shaped role clarity, coordination, accountability, and stakeholder ownership, while economic factors influenced the feasibility, timing, scale, and equity of preparedness, response, recovery, and learning-continuity measures. The synthesis indicated that resilience planning was more effective when School Improvement Planning, DRRM/CCA/EiE integration, learning-continuity planning, risk data, teacher capacity building, learner participation, psychosocial support, and resilient infrastructure were treated as connected planning mechanisms rather than separate compliance requirements. The study developed an integrated political-economic framework for secondary-school resilience and recommended future mixed-method, multi-site, and participatory research linking policy implementation, school finance, hazard exposure, and learning-continuity outcomes.

title: Can Language Models Identify Shadow Trading Targets? An NLP Evaluation of SEC Enforcement Theory
affiliations: , Columbia University, Columbia University and Columbia University

detail.title: Can Language Models Identify Shadow Trading Targets? An NLP Evaluation of SEC Enforcement Theory
detail.abstract: Shadow trading -- trading in a peer firm's securities on the basis of material nonpublic information (MNPI) about an "economically linked" company -- is a novel and contested theory of insider trading liability, first prosecuted in SEC v. Panuwat (2023). Enforcing it requires identifying economically linked firms ex ante, a determination the SEC makes only after the fact using mass market surveillance infrastructure. We ask whether NLP can do what the SEC's theory presumes insiders already know: identify peer firms ex ante from publicly mandated disclosures. Using a two-stage LLM pipeline applied to Item 7 (Management's Discussion and Analysis) sections of SEC 10-K filings, we score semantic similarity across 30 M&A events spanning five industries and relate similarity to announcement-day abnormal stock returns. On the Panuwat fact pattern itself the pipeline recovers Incyte among the closest peers, a sanity check on the one case with a known outcome. Across the full dataset, however, we find no association: pooling 217 peer observations, the within-event rank correlation between similarity and abnormal return is +0.07 (permutation p = 0.37), and the mean per-event Spearman correlation is +0.05 with a 95% confidence interval of [-0.08, +0.18] -- narrow enough to exclude any moderate relationship rather than merely failing to detect one. A case-level reading agrees: 14 of 30 events support the hypothesis, 12 contradict it, and 4 are ambiguous. We also find that Incyte fell outside the standard $2B-$10B mid-cap band on the day before the announcement, complicating the "mid-cap oncology" category the SEC invoked. These results are exploratory and bound to this pipeline, corpus, and return measure, but they put pressure on the empirical premise of shadow trading enforcement and bear on constitutional questions surrounding the SEC's financial surveillance infrastructure.

title: All in the Family: Family Offices and the Limits of Financial Regulation
affiliations: Washington and Lee University School of Law

detail.title: All in the Family: Family Offices and the Limits of Financial Regulation
detail.abstract:
Family offices have quietly become major actors in modern financial markets while remaining largely outside the scope of financial regulation. While financial regulation is typically focused on investor protection, family offices invert that premise. Instead, family offices manage the high net worth wealth of families and as sophisticated investors, have no need for investor protection. Therefore, family offices are broadly exempt from registration, disclosure, and oversight under the Investment Advisers Act. Yet many family offices deploy capital at a scale and with a degree of leverage and interconnectedness that rivals regulated institutions. 

This Article argues that the family office exemption reveals a structural mismatch in financial regulation: a regime built on investor protection confronting entities for whom investor protection is largely irrelevant, but whose activities may nonetheless generate systemic risk. The 2021 collapse of Archegos Capital Management underscores how opacity and leverage within a single family office can transmit losses across major financial institutions without regulators having any ability to see any of it. 

At the same time, extending full scale regulation to family offices risks undermining the very features that justify the family office model, including long term investment horizons, flexibility, and privacy. This Article contends that the rise of family offices exposes the limits of entity based regulation in an era of financial innovation and regulatory arbitrage. Regulation should therefore shift toward an activity-based approach and targeted reporting obligations, especially as family offices continue to grow in size and scope.

title: Narrative Authority: A Foundational Construct of Narrative Power Leadership Theory - Why Leaders Lose Influence before they Lose Position

detail.title: Narrative Authority: A Foundational Construct of Narrative Power Leadership Theory - Why Leaders Lose Influence before they Lose Position

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the research, authorship, or publication of this working paper. The views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a conceptual theoretical work based on analysis of existing scholarly literature. It did not involve human participants, identifiable personal data, or animal subjects. Accordingly, institutional ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Leadership scholars have long examined authority, legitimacy, and organizational influence, yet comparatively little attention has been devoted to explaining why leaders frequently lose influence before losing their formal positions. This working paper introduces Narrative Authority as a foundational construct of Narrative Power Leadership Theory (NPLT). Narrative Authority is defined as the degree to which followers accept a leader's interpretation of reality as credible, legitimate, and worthy of action. Drawing on foundational scholarship in narrative, sensemaking, legitimacy, and framing, the paper argues that leadership influence depends not only on institutional authority but also on a leader's continuing ability to shape shared interpretations during uncertainty. The paper distinguishes narrative authority from positional authority and identifies its theoretical contribution to leadership research.

title: Beyond Exponential Growth Bias: Principal Linearity Neglect in Savings Judgments
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School and University of California San Diego

detail.title: Beyond Exponential Growth Bias: Principal Linearity Neglect in Savings Judgments

declarations.ethicsApproval: The studies were approved by the IRBs of the authors' universities.

detail.abstract: Estimating the future value of an asset requires combining three components: principal, interest rate, and duration. Extensive research documents how people underestimate exponential growth as duration increases (exponential growth bias). We identify a complementary error: people also underestimate the linear relationship between principal and future value. We term this misperception principal linearity neglect (PLN). Across four preregistered experiments where participants estimated final values of hypothetical retirement savings accounts (N = 3,876, Nobs = 20,370), participants underweighted the principal’s contribution to the final value by approximately 10%. This bias operated independently of exponential growth bias. Three converging findings are consistent with compressed magnitude representation as a plausible mechanism. First, PLN was attenuated less than exponential growth bias by financial literacy, numeracy, and decision time. Second, principal–future value relationships followed a power law consistent with Stevens’s (1957) psychophysical scaling. Finally, flexible functional forms improved model fit for exponential growth bias but not PLN. These findings suggest that errors in compound interest estimation arise from perceptual compression of numerical magnitudes – not just from errors in computation.

title: Designing Around Selection: Identification and Inference Under Multi-Dimensional Unobserved Heterogeneity
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School, University of Chicago - Department of Economics, Lyft, Inc. and Washington University in St. Louis

detail.title: Designing Around Selection: Identification and Inference Under Multi-Dimensional Unobserved Heterogeneity
detail.abstract: We study identification and optimal policy design in a broad class of principal-agent models. We show that the most common empirical framework within the literature is equivalent to an unstructured potential-outcomes model augmented with three specific assumptions: the Law of Demand (LoD), or treatment-effect monotonicity; extrapolative model structure (EMS), which rules out lumpy agent responses to price changes; and rank invariance (RI), which restricts unobserved heterogeneity (UH) to be one-dimensional. This decomposition isolates the identifying content of each assumption and clarifies its economic role. The LoD and MS are empirically testable using exogenous price variation; RI, on the other hand, is a strong assumption ruling out many economically plausible behaviors, and also not empirically testable. We derive sharp bounds on counterfactual outcomes when RI is relaxed. The conventional 1-dimensional model delivers an upper bound on planner objectives, while the lower bound, which allows for arbitrary multidimensional UH, has an adversarial interpretation for policy design. We estimate empirical bounds and apply them to nonlinear pricing of rideshare services. The resulting robust pricing policy fully insures against worst-case latent selection while preserving most of the profit and consumer-surplus gains predicted by the conventional model. Our framework provides a tractable approach to robust policy design in adverse-selection settings including Mirrleesian taxation, regulation, labor supply, and procurement.

title: Linking Inputs to Network Dimensions in Purpose-Oriented Networks
affiliations: , University of Illinois at Chicago, , Penn State Harrisburg and Georgia Institute of Technology

detail.title: Linking Inputs to Network Dimensions in Purpose-Oriented Networks
detail.abstract: The literature on purpose-oriented networks (PONs) has predominantly treated network structure as a predictor of network effectiveness. This paper reverses that analytical direction, treating a PON's internal relational structure (the pattern of ties among its member organizations) as the outcome to be explained. While research has established that network structure matters for what PONs accomplish, comparatively little work examines what institutional and contextual conditions give rise to different relational patterns. We address this gap by developing a framework linking five input variables, purpose, organizational capacity and resource munificence, degree of mandate, and external stability, to three network dimensions: structure, composition, and dynamics. For each input, we define the concept, review its operationalization, and develop directional propositions about how it shapes the network dimensions of a PON. The resulting propositions offer a foundation for future research and practical guidance for network design and intervention.

title: Drug-Induced Homicide: Defense Attorney Experiences and Case Characteristics in the United States
affiliations: North Carolina State University, Wayne State University Law School and Wayne State University Law School

detail.title: Drug-Induced Homicide: Defense Attorney Experiences and Case Characteristics in the United States

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no conflicts of interest to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research was administratively reviewed and determined to be exempt from further review by the Institutional Review Board at North Carolina State University
declarations.funderStatement: Research reported in this publication was supported by the National Institute On Drug Abuse of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number K01DA057414. The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health.

detail.abstract:
Drug-induced homicide (DIH) laws treat the delivery of a substance that contributes to a fatal overdose as a form of homicide. We surveyed criminal defense attorneys with experience defending against DIH charges (n=81) in 28 states to explore their professional experiences with and perceptions of DIH.

Respondents predominantly reported that DIH prosecutions were brought in response to fentanyl-involved deaths and contingent on clear evidence establishing that the defendant gave the deceased the drug that could have contributed to their death. Most agreed that charges engendered net negative consequences for the wider community. The vast majority (93.5%) of respondents reported their most recent DIH client was charged with the death of a White person, suggesting that DIH enforcement may reflect racialized judgments about which overdose deaths are treated as warranting criminal punishment. This study contributes to a growing literature considering how social discourses of Whiteness shape the U.S. War on Drugs.

title: Scenario-based Foresight of Agricultural Mechanization In Boroujerd County, Iran: Status Assessment, Key Drivers and Alternative Futures
affiliations: University of Tehran, University of Tehran and University of Tehran

detail.title: Scenario-based Foresight of Agricultural Mechanization In Boroujerd County, Iran: Status Assessment, Key Drivers and Alternative Futures
detail.abstract: Agricultural mechanization plays a critical role in enhancing productivity, reducing labor bottlenecks, and supporting sustainable agricultural transformation. However, less is known about how its future develops under uncertainty in local and region-specific contexts. This study presents a scenario-based foresight analysis of agricultural mechanization in Boroujerd County, Iran, with the aim of assessing the current status, identifying key drivers, and constructing alternative futures. A multi-stage methodological framework was employed. First, 73 variables related to mechanization were identified through literature review and expert consultation, and 64 were retained after validation and importance screening. These variables were then organized into six thematic groups and analyzed using MICMAC structural analysis to examine direct and indirect influence relationships. Based on influence-dependence potential, indirect influence, and direct influence, 19 key descriptors were selected for scenario development. Scenario Wizard was subsequently used to generate four internally consistent futures: preferable, probable, plausible, and possible. The findings show that agricultural mechanization in Boroujerd County is not driven by a single factor but by a dynamic structure of interdependent variables, among which institutional coordination, service accessibility, and technical capacity exert the greatest leverage. The study demonstrates that scenario planning is a useful approach for understanding mechanization futures under uncertainty and provides a strategic basis for long-term policy design. Overall, the research contributes to futures studies by offering a subnational, system-oriented, and policy-relevant analysis of agricultural mechanization.

title: SPORD: A Simulation-Propose-then-OR-Dispose Approach for Supply Chain Planning
affiliations: , JD.com Smart Supply Chain Y, JD.com Smart Supply Chain Y, JD.com Smart Supply Chain Y, JD.com Smart Supply Chain Y, JD.com Smart Supply Chain Y, Tsinghua University and University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: SPORD: A Simulation-Propose-then-OR-Dispose Approach for Supply Chain Planning
detail.abstract: For years, supply chain planning at e-commerce firms has operated as a collection of isolated projects. Each planning task from static network planning to dynamic warehouse assortment planning requires analysts to spend weeks building models from scratch, calibrating and persuading executives to act on outputs they cannot verify. Three barriers drive this: bespoke models proliferate because standardization is difficult (operational fragmentation); once unified, the combinatorial scale of millions of SKUs, thousands of nodes, and intricate routing logic exceeds what solvers can handle within a tight window (computational intractability); and a mathematically optimal solution still fails to be implemented if the executives do not trust it (implementation hurdle). To bridge this gap, we propose and implement the Simulation-Propose-then-OR-Dispose method, deployed as JD.com’s NetSim platform. The central insight is decoupling: simulation proposes by generating and evaluating the full set of operationally valid candidate paths-absorbing all idiosyncratic business logic, while an integer program disposes by selecting the globally optimal subset. Computationally, matrix-vectorized CPU/GPU accelerated simulation achieves a 10-100 times speedup over serial methods, and a list scheduling algorithm reduces coupled-order processing from hours to minutes. Operationally, we establish a closed loop via an intelligent diagnosis engine. Since 2025, NetSim has optimized end to-end services for over 20,000 suppliers, the cross-regional fulfillment rate dropped from 6.1% to 4.9%, and the average monthly carbon reduction is approximately 5,745 tCO2e. SPORD moves simulation from monitoring to active planning. The transparent outputs turn skeptical executives into engaged collaborators, and the modular architecture ensures that the next planning requires just configuration, not reconstruction.

title: Empowering the Telecom Workforce Mitigating Insider Threats in Telecommunications Espionage through Socio-Economic Improvements
affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University - Heinz College

detail.title: Empowering the Telecom Workforce Mitigating Insider Threats in Telecommunications Espionage through Socio-Economic Improvements
detail.abstract: Insider threats continue to plague organizations with reports continuing to show that trends of attacks are only rising since 2023. Despite technological advances and continual process modification in an effort to thwart these threats like "Zero Trust" architecture, increasing attacks show that these methods are not enough to thwart attempts. Research into the subject shows that insider threats have long standing commonalities with historical practices in espionage and sabotage recruitment efforts that often have attribution to negative socioeconomic conditions. These same conditions can lead to dire consequences for telecommunications and other organizations as these insiders have the knowledge of the intricate security processes and mechanisms of the organizations while also having the opportunity to seize opportunities to conduct espionage and sabotage. This thesis explores historical facets of insiders correlated to economic and political espionage, with modern-day telecommunications and other organizations. We then explore and connect military principles and strategies to these mechanisms-ultimately concluding that insiders can only be detected and defeated through the cultivation of holistic work practices and cultures.

title: Blue Gold: An Unfiltered Look at the Resource We Can't Live Without and the Crisis We Can't Afford to Ignore

detail.title: Blue Gold: An Unfiltered Look at the Resource We Can't Live Without and the Crisis We Can't Afford to Ignore

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently with no financial relationships with any organizations that could be perceived to have influenced the findings.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper contains no human subjects research, patient data, or clinical trials. All data referenced is sourced from publicly available datasets and published reports.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded as independent research.

detail.abstract: Between 2002 and 2024, satellite gravity measurements from NASA's GRACE and GRACE-FO missions recorded the loss of roughly 1,200 cubic kilometers of freshwater from the world's largest aquifers, river basins and ice reserves. To put that number in human terms, it is enough water to fill Lake Erie more than twice over, or to supply every household in the United States for close to a decade. This loss is not a slow, symmetric drawdown. It is concentrated in a handful of basins that grow a large share of the planet's food and host hundreds of millions of people, and it is accelerating. The financial exposure is larger than most investors realize. The World Bank and the World Resources Institute estimate that global GDP exposed to high water stress will rise from roughly $15 trillion in 2010 to as much as $70 trillion by 2050-a sum comparable to the combined annual output of the United States, China and the European Union today. Water touches semiconductor fabrication, thermal power generation, beverage manufacturing, data center cooling and municipal credit markets alike, which means a shock to water availability is rarely a single-sector event. Despite that exposure, water is arguably the most mispriced major resource on earth. Oil, natural gas and agricultural commodities all trade on liquid futures markets that let producers and consumers hedge years in advance. Water does not. A single, thinly traded California water futures contract represents the entire formal financial market for a resource more essential than any of them. This paper calls that gap the mispricing paradox: the commodity that makes every other commodity possible has almost no price discovery mechanism at all. This paper's purpose is twofold. First, to lay out the physical, financial and geopolitical dimensions of the crisis in plain language, with the data and the human-scale comparisons that let a non-specialist reader grasp the stakes. Second, and just as important, to make the case for optimism grounded in evidence: desalination costs have fallen more than 90 percent since the 1970s, wastewater recycling capacity has more than doubled in two decades, and capital is beginning to move. The technology and the money to solve this problem already exist.

title: Baqir's Nine Dimensions of Product Quality: Extending Garvin's Framework with Environmental Sustainability

detail.title: Baqir's Nine Dimensions of Product Quality: Extending Garvin's Framework with Environmental Sustainability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual paper and does not involve human participants or primary data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: David Garvin's 1987 framework of eight dimensions of product quality-performance, features, reliability, conformance, durability, serviceability, aesthetics, and perceived quality-remains the dominant vocabulary for describing product quality in both academic and applied quality management. The framework was built for a manufacturing economy in which environmental cost was externalized and rarely part of a buyer's quality judgment. That assumption no longer holds. Regulatory frameworks built on the life cycle perspective, buyer expectations shaped by climate awareness, and quality standards that now formally incorporate environmental management have together created a gap in Garvin's taxonomy. This paper proposes a ninth dimension-Environmental Sustainability-defined as the measurable environmental footprint of a product across its life cycle, from raw material extraction through use to disposal or recovery. The paper defines the dimension, grounds its necessity in the climate and regulatory record since 1987, and demonstrates that it is conceptually distinct from each of Garvin's existing eight dimensions rather than a restatement of durability, conformance, or serviceability under a different name.

title: Application of the Okishio-Type Capital Accumulation Model to AI Investment -An Analysis of Cumulative Disequilibrium Processes and Investment Reversal Thresholds
affiliations: Rodem Asset Co.,Ltd. CEO

detail.title: Application of the Okishio-Type Capital Accumulation Model to AI Investment -An Analysis of Cumulative Disequilibrium Processes and Investment Reversal Thresholds
detail.abstract: Based on Nobuo Okishio's theory of capital accumulation, this paper constructs one-sector and two-sector dynamic models utilizing Harrod-Okishio investment functions. First, in the one-sector model, we show the instability of the warranted growth path and clarify the conditions under which an upward cumulative process occurs. Next, expanding to a two-sector model, we formalize the mechanism of cumulative inter-sectoral disequilibrium. Furthermore, by introducing physical constraints (electricity and construction upper bounds) into Sector 1, we explicitly derive the thresholds at which investment reverses. Finally, applying these results to AI infrastructure investment in the mid-2020s, we argue that the current phase is in an upward cumulative process and that reversal risks are rising due to the manifestation of physical constraints.

title: Modified SERVQUAL: Adding Recovery Quality (Extending the RATER Framework with a Sixth, Post-Failure Dimension)

detail.title: Modified SERVQUAL: Adding Recovery Quality (Extending the RATER Framework with a Sixth, Post-Failure Dimension)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual paper proposing a theoretical extension to the SERVQUAL model; it does not involve human participants, patient data, or empirical data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The SERVQUAL model, developed by Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, has for nearly four decades organized service quality around five dimensions summarized by the acronym RATER: Reliability, Assurance, Tangibles, Empathy, and Responsiveness. These five dimensions describe how well a service is delivered, but none of them describe what happens after a service failure has already occurred. This paper argues that the RATER framework is systematically silent on a distinct and measurable moment in the service encounter, service recovery, and proposes Recovery Quality as a sixth dimension. The proposal is positioned against two bodies of prior work it is most easily mistaken for, Berry, Parasuraman, and Zeithaml's Service Quality Ring, which treated recovery as a management lesson rather than a measurable customer-perceived dimension, and context-specific replacement scales such as the Retail Service Quality Scale, which bolt on an ad hoc dimension for one industry rather than extending RATER generally. Recovery Quality is then defined, distinguished from Reliability, Responsiveness, and Assurance to establish non-overlap, and grounded in the service recovery paradox literature, which shows that a wellhandled failure can leave a customer more satisfied than if no failure had occurred at all. The paper concludes with implications for how service organizations measure quality and directions for empirical validation of the proposed dimension.

title: Reversibility as a Factor of Production - A General Theory of the Economics of Error

detail.title: Reversibility as a Factor of Production - A General Theory of the Economics of Error
detail.abstract:
This article introduces reversibility as a factor of production in its own right. Reversibility is the efficiency with which an economy converts its failures into reusable knowledge while preserving the capacity of agents to try again.

A coefficient Rho between 0 and 1, decomposable into five components mounted in series — financial, legal, social, cognitive and political — governs three channels: the accumulation of an unmeasured stock of experience capital; the volume of experimentation, through an entry threshold that rationalizes the observed prudence of poor economies; and the depth of hysteresis after shocks.

The interaction of these three channels generates a conformity trap, whose geometry is that of the “cusp catastrophe” and whose early-warning signals are refutable.

It also generates an asymmetric law of belief adjustment, the law of freeze and thaw, which we microfound as the exact nonlinear filtering of a hidden institutional regime.

On this basis, the article establishes an aggregation theorem for a Reversibility Index; an all-or-nothing optimal-reform result, the clean-jump theorem; and a series of amendments to canonical theories — Ricardian trade, the Phillips curve, Modigliani–Miller, the Keynesian multiplier, loss aversion, Eaton–Gersovitz sovereign debt, Holmström–Milgrom contracts — each of which is recovered exactly in the limit Rho tends towards 1.

The construction closes with a general theory: five axioms; an invariant that is the institutional analogue of the Carnot bound; a McKean–Vlasov field equation for the distribution of beliefs; a notion of economic proper time whose dilation defines underdevelopment; and a correspondence principle that makes received economic theory the zeroth-order term of an expansion in (1-Rho).

title: Construction of Audit Evidence Chain and SOX Control Verification Mechanism for Transaction -level Financial Data in High Volume E -commerce Platform
affiliations: Columbia University, Johns Hopkins University, University of College London and George Washington University

detail.title: Construction of Audit Evidence Chain and SOX Control Verification Mechanism for Transaction -level Financial Data in High Volume E -commerce Platform
detail.abstract: Order, refund, settlement, tax and revenue-recognition data in high-volume e-commerce platforms are dispersed across source systems, transformation jobs and reporting layers. Typical lineage tools capture table dependency or pipeline lineage, but they are not typically tied to each transaction record, SOX control points, rule-validation results and audit samples. To fill this gap of transaction-level control testing, an audit evidence chain framework for financial details was built. Records in source tables, SQL logic in transformations, Airflow tasks, quality rules, and control points and report fields were organized into a data-lineage graph. GAT was used to identify high-risk lineage nodes, Great Expectations was used for rule validation, and LightGBM was used to predict SOX control anomalies. The dataset contains more than 10 million monthly orders, 260 core tables, 1200 report fields and 240 million job logs. Based on historical replay of production-scale logs, the results indicate that sample tracing time was reduced from 5.6 hours to 38 minutes, field-drift discovery time was reduced to 4.8 hours, GAT precision was improved to 93.1%, and LightGBM AUC was improved to 0.927. The framework provides for evidence tracing at the transaction level and control verification for SOX, but the review of the judgment and remediation is still being done manually for high volume financial data.

title: Risk Aversion in the Small and in the Large: Beyond Arrow-Pratt A Wiener Chaos Hierarchy of Dynamic Risk Premia
affiliations: University of Glasgow

detail.title: Risk Aversion in the Small and in the Large: Beyond Arrow-Pratt A Wiener Chaos Hierarchy of Dynamic Risk Premia
detail.abstract: The Arrow-Pratt approximation is one of the cornerstones of expected utility theory, providing the classical local approximation of certainty equivalents and risk premia in terms of absolute risk aversion. Despite its widespread use, its mathematical scope and relationship to higher-order risk preferences remain only partially understood. This paper develops a new framework for the analysis of certainty equivalents and dynamic risk premia based on Malliavin calculus and Wiener chaos analysis. We first show that the classical Arrow-Pratt approximation is not asymptotically valid for arbitrary sequences of vanishing risks, thereby identifying precise limitations of the traditional theory. Motivated by this observation, we formulate certainty equivalents dynamically by considering the progressive revelation of uncertainty through a Brownian filtration. Combining Itô calculus, the Clark-Ocone representation and the Wiener chaos decomposition, we derive a complete hierarchy of higher-order dynamic risk premia and obtain explicit representations of the corresponding coefficients in terms of Malliavin derivatives. For mixed Wiener chaos expansions, higher-order preference measures, including prudence and temperance, emerge naturally through interactions between chaos components and are characterised using Bell polynomial representations. Explicit results for quadratic Gaussian functionals and the Vasicek interest-rate model illustrate the theory and identify a broad class of regular Wiener functionals for which the classical Arrow-Pratt approximation is recovered as the leading-order term. The results establish a unified framework linking expected utility theory, stochastic analysis and Wiener chaos expansions, opening a new perspective on higher-order certainty equivalents and the dynamic measurement of risk.

title: Psychometric properties of the short version of the Perceived Organizational Dehumanization Scale (PODS-8): A diagnostic tool for educational administration in Peru
affiliations: Universidad Peruana Union, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidad Peruana Union

detail.title: Psychometric properties of the short version of the Perceived Organizational Dehumanization Scale (PODS-8): A diagnostic tool for educational administration in Peru
detail.abstract: Despite the growing attention given to teachers' psychosocial working conditions, perceived organizational dehumanization remains an understudied concept in educational settings due to a lack of psychometrically robust instruments. Therefore, this study aimed to translate, adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Perceived Organizational Dehumanization Scale (PODS-8). An instrumental study was conducted with 410 Peruvian teachers of Regular Basic Education, representative of the three regions of Peru (coast, highlands, and jungle). Participants were between 19 and 65 years old (M = 35.41 and SD = 10.23). The analyses used structural equation modeling (SEM) with the AMOS 24 statistical software. Confirmatory factor analysis yielded an 8-item unifactorial fit model (CMIN/DF = 3.509; CFI = 0.991; SRMR = 0.012; RMSEA = 0.078; and Pclose = 0.015). The results demonstrated good internal consistency. PODS-8 confirmed positive and significant associations with related constructs (job insecurity and job burnout). The Spanish version of the PODS-8 is positioned as a valid and reliable tool for assessing dehumanization in basic education organizations. This study contributes to the scientific field and important areas such as organizational psychology and human talent management in the education sector, thus providing a diagnostic tool for educational administration in Peru.

title: Forecastability and Cost Structure: The Effect of Forecasted Sales Changes and Demand Uncertainty
affiliations: Osaka Metropolitan University, Kindai University,  and

detail.title: Forecastability and Cost Structure: The Effect of Forecasted Sales Changes and Demand Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Firms routinely face demand fluctuations that differ in their degree of forecastability, yet prior studies measure demand uncertainty using aggregate sales volatility, conflating forecastable variation with unforecastable shocks. We argue that these two components lead to fundamentally different capacity and cost structure decisions. We develop an analytical model showing that unforecastable demand shocks increase the value of committed capacity, resulting in a more rigid cost structure, whereas forecastable demand variation enables firms to rely on flexible resources and maintain greater cost elasticity. The model further predicts that cost responses to unexpected favorable demand shocks are weaker than responses to comparable planned demand increases because capacity is committed ex ante. We test these predictions using Japanese listed firms, whose mandatory management sales forecasts allow us to decompose realized sales changes into forecastable variation and unforecastable forecast errors. Using 44,021 firm-year observations from 1997 to 2023, we find that unforecastable demand variation is associated with lower cost elasticity across SG&A, cost of goods sold, and employment, while forecastable demand variation increases cost elasticity for SG&A and employment. We also find that firms respond less aggressively to unexpected favorable demand shocks than to comparable planned demand increases, consistent with binding capacity constraints. Our findings reconcile competing predictions in the cost structure literature by demonstrating that the operational consequences of demand uncertainty depend on its forecastability and highlight demand forecasting as an important determinant of capacity commitment and operational flexibility.

title: Improving Existing Protected areas could Double their Modelled Threat-Reduction Impact
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome, University of Texas at Dallas - School of Economic, Political and Policy Sciences and Sapienza University of Rome - Global Mammal Assessment Program

detail.title: Improving Existing Protected areas could Double their Modelled Threat-Reduction Impact

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: C.V. thanks the Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research, Programma Operativo Nazionale (CUP B85F21005360001) for funding her research activities.

detail.abstract: Biodiversity is essential for ecosystem stability and human well-being, but human activities have intensified pressures on nature, leading to biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation. Protected areas are considered an effective instrument for safeguarding biodiversity and are among the most widely used conservation strategies worldwide, yet assessing their ability to reduce human pressures remains difficult as it requires disentangling the effects of protection from confounding factors such as location and accessibility. Here we estimate average treatment effects on terrestrial protected areas for fourteen spatial threat indicators and an overall composite index using a quasi-experimental approach. We find that the composite index is 31.5% lower for protected pixels than in matched controls, with statistically significant reductions in built area, cropland, mining, roads, powerlines, and forest loss. Threat reductions are strongest in tropical forests, where protected areas reduce threats at nearly twice the global average. Assuming that not all protected areas can eliminate all threats, we use the best-performing protected areas within comparable pressure contexts as a benchmark and estimate that existing protected areas achieve 49.2% of their model-implied, area-weighted threat-reduction potential. Furthermore, our results show that many threatened vertebrate ranges remain exposed to ongoing pressure even inside protected areas. Our analysis shows considerable room for improvement in the management of existing protected areas, and provides a decision-support framework that balances protection expansion with improvements in effectiveness to achieve the Convention on Biological Diversity's protected area target.

title: Enterprise Development through Women's Collectives: Experimental Evidence from Rural India
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Enterprise Development through Women's Collectives: Experimental Evidence from Rural India
detail.abstract: Female entrepreneurship remains constrained by multiple market and social barriers, yet there is limited causal evidence on whether enterprise development programmes delivered through women's collectives can overcome these constraints. We evaluate a multi-component enterprise development programme that combines business training, postharvest processing, value addition, and market linkage support for women's self-help groups engaged in millet value chains in Odisha, India. The programme was evaluated using a three-arm cluster randomised controlled trial that separately identifies the effects of postharvest processing support and commercially oriented value-addition training. Commercially oriented value-addition training substantially increased female enterprise creation, startup investment, business revenues, and profits, whereas postharvest processing support alone generated little measurable impact on entrepreneurial outcomes. The intervention also improved women's empowerment, increasing participation in entrepreneurial decision-making, strengthening control over income, and reducing work hours. The results suggest that general business training alone is insufficient to stimulate female entrepreneurship. Rather, combining technical skills with commercially viable product development and market opportunities relaxes multiple constraints simultaneously and enables women to establish profitable enterprises. These findings contribute new causal evidence that integrating value addition into agricultural value chains can promote both female entrepreneurship and women's economic empowerment, with important implications for the design of enterprise development programmes in low-income settings.

title: The Impact of Short-Video Content on the Impulse Buying Behavior of University Students in Pakistan

detail.title: The Impact of Short-Video Content on the Impulse Buying Behavior of University Students in Pakistan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with any individual or organization that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: As this was an independent undergraduate research project rather than an institutionally-funded study, formal ethics board (IRB) approval was not sought. However, participant safety and rights were maintained throughout: participation was entirely voluntary and anonymous, no personally identifying information was collected, and respondents gave implied consent by choosing to complete the survey.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was self-funded by the author as part of an independent undergraduate research project.

detail.abstract:
The fast emergence of short video platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts has led to a drastic change in the manner in which younger consumers identify and assess products. The current study examines the effect of short video content on the impulsive purchase decisions of Pakistani university students, an understudied context compared to the East and Southeast Asian context, which have been studied more extensively thus far. Based on the S-O-R theoretical perspective, the study considers short video content features, which include visually stimulating material, influencers’ credibility, celebrities' endorsements, promotion, and FOMO, as stimuli to consumer impulses.

This study adopted a quantitative cross-sectional survey research design. The data was collected from 122 university students of Pakistan via an online survey employing the 5-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, reliability, correlation and regression analyses were used to analyze the collected data. The findings indicate that there is a strong positive and statistically significant association between the content-exposure and impulse buying behavior (r = .722, p < .001), with the model accounting for about 52% of the variance in impulse buying behavior (R² = .522). The content-exposure scale (α = .919) and impulse buying behavior scale (α = .810) both showed high internal consistency. Promotional cues and celebrity endorsement were the two most important variables predicting impulsive buying behavior.

The results support the assertion that short videos can act as strong behavior stimulators among Pakistani university students, providing insight into marketing strategies and the financial benefits of consumers. This paper ends with the recommendation of future directions, which include mediating psychological factors and larger sample sizes.

title: What Do Firm-Level AI Measures Measure? Disclosure, Selection, and the Employment Effects of Generative AI
affiliations: and Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University)

detail.title: What Do Firm-Level AI Measures Measure? Disclosure, Selection, and the Employment Effects of Generative AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
Firm-level measures of corporate AI built from 10-K text are increasingly used to study how artificial intelligence affects labor, yet what they capture is unclear. We build a public, full-window (2018–2025) generative-AI disclosure measure for a Russell 3000-scale panel of large US public firms and audit it. About a quarter of the firm-years it flags mention generative AI only as a risk rather than as something the firm does, and an independent language-model reading of the filings confirms that the measure conflates genuine adopters with firms naming the technology as a threat. The measure is a noisy, endogenous proxy for adoption.
We then show that this matters for inference. We pair the measure with a predetermined-exposure design that weights each firm’s pre-shock occupation mix by occupation-level language-model exposure and interacts it with the November 2022 ChatGPT shock.
The negative adoption-employment correlation that animates the displacement narrative disappears under this design: it reflects selection, because the firms that adopt were already on different employment paths. Exposure is also nearly collinear with the workforce’s remote-work capability, a twin that biases naive estimates toward displacement, so the null we report is conservative.
Applied to the first-order question, the cleaned design shows that generative-AI exposure has not displaced net employment through fiscal 2025. The absence of displacement is precise rather than merely undetected, uniform across industry sectors,
and echoed by the secondary margins (productivity, revenue, margins, mass layoffs, and firm value). Our contribution is a validated, reusable measure of corporate generative-AI engagement, a measurement-and-identification caution for a literature that increasingly reads firm-level AI correlations as causal, and firm-level evidence that generative AI has not displaced the corporate workforce.

title: DYNAMICS-8: An Eight Dimension Personality Framework for Computational Behavioural Simulation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: DYNAMICS-8: An Eight Dimension Personality Framework for Computational Behavioural Simulation

declarations.funderStatement: Self funded

detail.abstract: We present DYNAMICS-8, an eight dimension continuous personality framework designed for computational behavioural simulation. DYNAMICS-8 retains six dimensions grounded in thirty years of validated personality science (the Big Five and HEXACO models) and introduces two built for this purpose dimensions: Acuity (digital fluency and platform nativeness) and Impulsivity (delay discounting and reward sensitivity). Unlike the Big Five and HEXACO, which optimise for internal consistency of self report questionnaires, DYNAMICS-8 optimises for predictive validity of observable behaviour in digital, financial, and social contexts. We define the framework formally: eight dimensions with four facets each (32 parameters), continuous 0.0-1.0 scoring, deterministic derivation mappings from personality to economic behaviour, political orientation, and interpersonal compatibility, and a census weighted persona generation methodology producing demographically representative synthetic populations. We validate the framework against a published dataset of 1,000 synthetic personas (500 UK, 500 US) with up to 187 behavioural fields per persona. Ten prespecified statistical tests confirm all hypotheses at Bonferroni corrected alpha (10 comparisons): Discipline predicts savings rate (d = 1.74), Mercuriality predicts emotional reactivity (d = 5.32), Sociability predicts relationship network size (d = 1.55), Impulsivity predicts impulse spending (d = 0.94) and price insensitivity (d = 0.78), Acuity predicts credit score (d = 0.22), Novelty predicts experience seeking behaviour (d = 0.44), Candour predicts brand loyalty (d = 0.21), Yielding predicts institutional trust (d = 0.54), and a Discipline and Impulsivity interaction test produces an emergent effect (d = 2.27) exceeding either single dimension. All p < 0.025, eight at p < 0.001. We demonstrate three downstream applications: synthetic consumer panel research, personality conditioned dialogue generation, and pairwise compatibility scoring with conflict prediction. The framework specification (CC BY 4.0), reference implementations in Python and Go (BSL 1.1), and the 1,000-persona validation dataset (CC BY-NC 4.0) are publicly available.

title: Financial Literacy, Trust, and Receptivity to AI Financial Advice: Evidence from the 2024 National Financial Capability Study

detail.title: Financial Literacy, Trust, and Receptivity to AI Financial Advice: Evidence from the 2024 National Financial Capability Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationships with other people or organisations that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required. This study is a secondary analysis of publicly available, de-identified survey data (the 2024 National Financial Capability Study, FINRA Investor Education Foundation). No participants were recruited, and no identifiable personal data were accessed by the author.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Who is open to receiving financial advice from artificial intelligence? Prior work on robo-advisory adoption reports a paradox in which subjective financial confidence, rather than objective competence, drives trust in algorithmic advice (Chen, Aw and Tan, 2025). This study provides a pre-registered test of that claim, derived from the Contextual Trust Calibration Framework (CTCF; Hari, 2026), using the first nationally representative United States measure of receptivity to AI financial advice: item B61 of the 2024 National Financial Capability Study (n = 25,539; analytic n = 18,102). The pre-registered prediction was not supported. Objective financial literacy is a strong positive predictor of interest in AI advice (OR = 1.24 per standard deviation), and the pre-specified equivalence test rejects the predicted null. In contrast, selfassessed knowledge shows no significant association, and day-today financial self-efficacy shows a small negative association. Generalised trust propensity predicts receptivity as hypothesised. Unexpectedly, respondents who believe they were targeted by financial fraud in the past year are considerably more interested in AI advice (OR = 1.63). A pre-registered test of a decision-stakes moderation (portfolio value × trust propensity) in the merged Investor Survey subsample (n = 2,006) shows no evidence of an interaction. The results indicate that the confidence-over-competence pattern documented among roboadvisory users does not generalise to stated receptivity in the general population, consistent with the CTCF's core claim that dispositional effects on trust in algorithmic advice are context-dependent.

title: Recruiting for Scarcity: A Soft-Systems Analysis of the Niche-Technology Skills Gap in the Indian IT Workforce, Revisited in the Generative-AI Era
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Recruiting for Scarcity: A Soft-Systems Analysis of the Niche-Technology Skills Gap in the Indian IT Workforce, Revisited in the Generative-AI Era
detail.abstract: This paper examines the recruitment and retention of niche-technology talent in the Indian information-technology (IT) sector using a soft-systems perspective. The analysis was originally developed as a management-consultancy coursework exercise in 2023, built on stakeholder mapping, Soft Systems Methodology (SSM), CATWOE analysis, and a BCG growth-share prioritisation of interventions. The present paper retains that conceptual architecture but reexamines it against 2025-2026 evidence on India's artificial-intelligence (AI) talent gap, IT-sector attrition, and the accelerating adoption of AI in hiring. The re-analysis finds that the structural conflict identified in 2023-IT firms and clients competing for a scarce pool of experienced, nicheskilled professionals, while candidates and hiring teams negotiate under asymmetric informationhas not resolved; if anything, the gap has narrowed in generality (fewer roles are affected) but sharpened in intensity (the affected roles, concentrated in AI, cloud, and data engineering, are harder to fill than before). The paper argues that AI has entered the system twice over: as a driver of the skills shortage (because AI-related roles are now the hardest to fill) and as a candidate solution to it (because AI-assisted screening, upskilling, and workforce analytics are now mainstream HR practice in India). The original recommendation-that firms should prioritise structured training of early-career talent over competing for scarce experienced hires-is reassessed against current evidence and found to remain broadly sound, with an added caveat that AI-literacy training must now be treated as a first-order component of that pipeline rather than an auxiliary skill. Declaration of Generative AI Use Generative AI tools were used under the author's supervision to support literature search and synthesis, drafting assistance, and formatting of this manuscript from the author's original 2023 coursework analysis. All conceptual frameworks, stakeholder judgements, and interpretive conclusions are the author's own. The author reviewed and takes full responsibility for the final content.

title: The Role of Food Delivery Applications and Social Media in Shaping Consumer Decision-Making and Food Purchasing Behaviour Among Generation Z in Mumbai

detail.title: The Role of Food Delivery Applications and Social Media in Shaping Consumer Decision-Making and Food Purchasing Behaviour Among Generation Z in Mumbai
